priority_questions: Separate exported collaboration from unauthorized disclosure.
Relate projection, grant mode, recipient, and selected provider.
projects.expected_assessment: The supplied sharing operation matches its preview/read contract. Exported status alone is not a defect; the finite EDIT denial is supported.
limits: No claim of every recipient or provider being safe.
Do not infer whole-directory access from one scoped grant.

priority_questions: Identify the incomplete installed split set.
Distinguish forwarding interface from selected feature implementation.
projects.expected_assessment: Import authorization is unresolved from the supplied base-only material. Neither absence of protection nor correctness follows.
limits: Ask for the owner-provided feature artifact or corresponding source and active binding.
No scanner verdict or recreated mock can stand in for that feature.

priority_questions: Relate job identity, creation account, and committed effect.
Separate contract discrepancy from inference about the worker root cause.
projects.expected_assessment: The supplied finite J19 record contradicts its account-binding contract. This is not proof which client/server implementation caused the discrepancy.
limits: No account takeover, duplicate effect, or production-wide consequence is established.
Selected worker and server source remain required for root-cause attribution.

priority_questions: Distinguish intended group membership from access by unrelated apps.
Compare field-level sharing promise with actual projection.
projects.expected_assessment: The supplied H41 collaboration is consistent with its declared group and field contract. The generic sandbox-failure assertion is unsupported.
limits: No statement about every group member or Keychain access group.
A file-sharing entitlement is not Keychain authorization.

priority_questions: Separate source plist, signed capabilities, and runtime state.
Identify simulator and incomplete distribution evidence.
projects.expected_assessment: The capability and network behavior questions remain unresolved. Decompilation failure does not establish absence; purpose text does not establish signed permission.
limits: Do not propose decryption or platform bypasses.
Use owner-supplied signed inspection, source, or suitable development evidence.

priority_questions: Separate local authentication policy from remote object permission.
Interpret actual backend denial rather than UI access alone.
projects.expected_assessment: The recorded fallback is intended, and the specific server approval was denied. No remote-approval bypass is established for L71.
limits: A denial for O is not proof of every server operation.
No per-transaction cryptographic binding can be inferred from this UI helper.

priority_questions: Distinguish protocol sharing from native implementation equivalence.
Identify units, snapshot ownership, and platform evidence.
projects.expected_assessment: The Android finite sample supports the snapshot/byte contract. iOS equivalence is unresolved; shared schema and version label do not settle it.
limits: No native memory-corruption or cross-platform defect is established.
Do not fabricate a replacement adapter to claim iOS behavior.

priority_questions: Bind observations to the build, trust store, and client.
Distinguish pinning from ordinary transport verification.
projects.expected_assessment: The supplied debug capture does not establish released trust failure. Missing optional pinning is not itself a violation of the stated transport contract; release verification behavior remains partly unresolved.
limits: Do not claim secure release behavior solely from a configuration declaration.
No pinning bypass, certificate installation, or live interception is required by this exercise.
